written: 2026-10-12, before any test-split result of any method was computed (only data layout, issue targets/root-cause labels listing, and PC timing on noissue data had been looked at)
prediction_P15: declared topology plus abstention beats learned-graph RCA on AC@3 by at least 0.1; refuted if the gap is under 0.03 (verbatim, not changed)

P15_operationalisation.primary: gap = AC@3 of (d) on answered test issues minus AC@3 of (b) over all test issues (tie-aware expected AC@3, pooled over the 48 test issues of the 4 scenarios). Counts only if (d) test coverage >= 0.5; otherwise the strict metric below is the verdict.
P15_operationalisation.strict: gap = AC@3 of (d) counting abstentions as misses minus AC@3 of (b). Reported alongside; if primary and strict verdicts differ, both are stated.
P15_operationalisation.verdict: supported if gap >= 0.10; refuted if gap < 0.03; inconclusive in between. Paired bootstrap 95% CI over test issues (2000 resamples, seed 20261012) is reported but does not change the verdict.

scoring.AC@k: 1 if the single true root-cause node is within the top k, else 0 (one root cause per issue, so AC@k = top-k recall of Hardt et al.); tie-aware: when the true node sits in a tie group straddling position k, the hit is the probability under a uniform random order of the tie group, clamp((k - a)/g, 0, 1), a = number of strictly better candidates, g = tie-group size. Primary metric is tie-aware; a name-ascending deterministic tie-break is reported for per-issue ranks only.
scoring.empty output: counts as a miss (as in the authors' evaluate())

abstention_rule.shape: abstain iff the candidate list is empty, or it has >= 4 candidates and the margin between the 3rd and 4th scores is <= tau (margin = 0 if s3 == s4; inf if s3 is inf and s4 finite; else (s3 - s4)/max(|s3|, 1e-12)), i.e. the top-3 set is not determined by the scores
abstention_rule.tuning: train split only (20 issues, all PetSearch root causes), per method: choose tau maximising tie-aware AC@3 on answered train issues subject to train coverage >= 0.5; ties -> smallest tau; if no tau reaches coverage 0.5, tau = 0
abstention_rule.applied_to: (d) declared traversal, (e) graph-free ranked correlation (decision uses the untruncated ranked list), plus an extra row (b+abstain) on the learned-graph traversal

learned_graph: PC (causal-learn 0.1.4.8), Fisher-z, alpha 0.05, stable=True, uc_rule 0, uc_priority 2, on the noissue period, one graph per (scenario, target metric) using the <metric>/Average column of every service; columns with < 10 non-missing values or zero std in the normal period are excluded from PC and enter the learned graph as isolated nodes; remaining NaNs mean-imputed. Undirected and bidirected PC edges count both ways (each end is a parent of the other; paths may use them in either direction) for the primary (b); a seeded random orientation of undirected edges is a sensitivity row. The acyclicity check of the authors' traversal is skipped on learned graphs (recorded).
declared_graph: graph.csv adjacency (A->B means A calls B), reversed into callee->caller as in baseline_anomaly_traversal.make_baseline_analyze_root_causes
anomaly_detection: authors' DEFAULT_ANOMALY_DETECTION: dowhy MedianDeviationScorer (|x - median| / statsmodels mad, i.e. MAD scaled by 1/0.6745) fitted per service on the noissue period, threshold 5; zero-std services use |x - mean| with threshold 0; < 10 points -> no detector; analysis row = 3rd row of the issue or the first later row where the target is anomalous
column_shuffle: one permutation of metric columns per scenario from numpy default_rng([20261012, scenario_index]); applied to noissue and issue files alike; (b) and (c) rerun (all methods rerun for completeness)
